paragraphs: The European Union wants to make online shopping fairer. A new plan is coming this week. Irish politician Michael McGrath wrote it. He works for the European Commission.

Ticket websites like Ticketmaster must show more information. They must say how many tickets are left. They must also show the price. People waiting in an online queue will see the price and the highest price.
Some apps give a free trial and then take money. Under the plan, companies must warn people first. Stopping a subscription online must be easy.
Games must show the chance of winning prizes in loot boxes. Users can also turn off endless scrolling and videos that play by themselves.
The plan is not a law yet. EU politicians and governments must agree first.
sentZh: 歐盟希望讓網路購物更公平。
一項新計畫將在本週推出。
愛爾蘭政治人物麥格拉斯撰寫了這項計畫。
他在歐盟執委會工作。
像Ticketmaster這樣的售票網站必須顯示更多資訊。
它們必須說明還剩多少張票。
它們也必須顯示票價。
在線上排隊的人將看到目前價格和最高價格。
有些應用程式提供免費試用，之後就收錢。
根據這項計畫，公司必須先提醒用戶。
在網路上取消訂閱必須很容易。
遊戲必須顯示戰利品箱中贏得獎品的機率。
用戶也可以關閉無限滾動和自動播放的影片。
這項計畫還不是法律。
歐盟的政治人物和各國政府必須先同意。

paragraphs: The European Commission is set to present new rules this week to protect people who shop online. The plan is called the Digital Fairness Act. It was prepared by Michael McGrath, the Irish commissioner in charge of consumer protection.

One big part of the plan is about concert and sports tickets. Websites such as Ticketmaster would have to tell buyers how many tickets are still available and how much they cost. People waiting in an online queue would see the current price and the highest possible price.

The rules would also cover subscriptions. Companies would have to warn customers before a free trial ends and they start paying, or before a contract renews automatically. Cancelling online would have to be simple.

Video games with loot boxes would need to show the chances of winning. Influencers could not make false claims that a product is good for the environment. Users would also be able to switch off features like endless scrolling and autoplay.
However, the plan is only a first step. Members of the European Parliament and EU governments must still discuss it and agree on it.
sentZh: 歐盟執委會本週將提出保護網路購物者的新規定。
這項計畫名為《數位公平法》。
它由負責消費者保護的愛爾蘭籍執委麥格拉斯擬定。
計畫的一大重點是演唱會和體育賽事門票。
像Ticketmaster這樣的網站必須告訴買家還有多少張票以及票價多少。
在線上排隊的人將看到目前價格和可能的最高價格。
這些規定也將涵蓋訂閱服務。
公司必須在免費試用結束、開始收費前，或合約自動續約前提醒顧客。
線上取消也必須簡單。
有戰利品箱的電子遊戲需要顯示中獎機率。
網紅不得虛假宣稱某產品對環境有益。
用戶也能關閉無限滾動和自動播放等功能。
不過，這項計畫只是第一步。
歐洲議會議員和歐盟各國政府仍須討論並達成共識。

paragraphs: The European Commission is due to unveil a major consumer protection package this week, aimed at making online markets more transparent. The proposed Digital Fairness Act has been drafted by Michael McGrath, Ireland's EU commissioner for justice and consumer protection.

Ticket sellers such as Ticketmaster are a key target. Under a draft seen by The Irish Times, sites would have to reveal how many tickets remain and at what price. Fans waiting in a virtual queue would be shown both the real-time price and the maximum price they could face. The proposal focuses on information, however, and does not ban dynamic pricing outright.

Subscription services would also face tighter obligations. Firms would have to alert customers before a free trial turns into a paid plan or before a contract renews automatically, and online cancellation would need to be straightforward.

Other measures target so-called dark patterns, such as fake warnings that stock is running out. Video game makers would have to publish the odds of winning loot box prizes, and influencers would be barred from making misleading green claims. Users would also gain the right to disable addictive features like infinite scroll and autoplay.
The proposal now goes to MEPs and member states, who can amend it before it becomes law.
sentZh: 歐盟執委會預計本週公布一套重大的消費者保護方案，旨在讓網路市場更透明。
擬議中的《數位公平法》由愛爾蘭籍歐盟司法暨消費者保護執委麥格拉斯起草。
Ticketmaster等售票業者是主要對象。
根據《愛爾蘭時報》看到的草案，網站必須公開還剩多少張票以及價格。
在虛擬隊伍中等待的歌迷將同時看到即時價格和可能面對的最高價格。
不過，這項提案著重於資訊揭露，並未全面禁止動態定價。
訂閱服務也將面臨更嚴格的義務。
企業必須在免費試用轉為付費方案或合約自動續約前提醒顧客，線上取消也必須簡便。
其他措施針對所謂的「黑暗模式」，例如假稱庫存即將售罄的警示。
遊戲開發商必須公布戰利品箱獎品的中獎機率，網紅也將被禁止發布誤導性的環保宣稱。
用戶還將有權關閉無限滾動和自動播放等容易上癮的功能。
提案接下來將交由歐洲議會議員和各成員國審議，他們可在成為法律前加以修改。

paragraphs: Brussels is poised to unveil a sweeping overhaul of online consumer law this week, in a move that could curb some of the most contentious practices in the digital economy. The Digital Fairness Act is the brainchild of Michael McGrath, the Irish commissioner who holds the justice and consumer protection brief.

Ticketing giants such as Ticketmaster are squarely in its sights. According to a draft obtained by The Irish Times, platforms would be compelled to disclose how many tickets are left and at what price. Fans languishing in a virtual queue would be entitled to see the prevailing price as well as the ceiling they might ultimately pay. Nevertheless, the measure stops short of outlawing dynamic pricing altogether.

Subscription providers, meanwhile, would be obliged to notify customers before a free trial lapses into a paid arrangement or a contract rolls over automatically. Withdrawing online would have to be hassle-free.

The draft also takes aim at manipulative design tricks, known as dark patterns, including bogus scarcity alerts. Games featuring loot boxes would have to spell out the probability of winning, and influencers would be forbidden from peddling spurious environmental claims. Users could also opt out of compulsive features such as infinite scroll and autoplay.
The proposal is merely the opening salvo, however. It must still run the gauntlet of the European Parliament and member states, both of which may amend it.
sentZh: 布魯塞爾本週準備公布網路消費者法的全面改革，此舉可能遏止數位經濟中一些最具爭議的做法。
《數位公平法》是愛爾蘭籍、主掌司法與消費者保護事務的執委麥格拉斯一手構想的。
Ticketmaster等售票巨頭首當其衝。
根據《愛爾蘭時報》取得的草案，平台將被迫公開剩餘票數及其價格。
在虛擬隊伍中苦等的歌迷，將有權看到當下價格以及最終可能支付的上限。
不過，這項措施並未完全禁止動態定價。
與此同時，訂閱服務業者必須在免費試用轉為付費方案、或合約自動續約之前通知顧客。
線上退訂也必須毫無麻煩。
草案也瞄準被稱為「黑暗模式」的操縱性設計伎倆，包括虛假的缺貨警示。
含有戰利品箱的遊戲必須清楚說明中獎機率，網紅也將被禁止兜售站不住腳的環保宣稱。
用戶還可選擇關閉無限滾動和自動播放等讓人欲罷不能的功能。
不過，這項提案只是第一槍。
它仍須通過歐洲議會和各成員國的重重考驗，兩者都可能修改內容。

paragraphs: The European Commission is expected to present the Digital Fairness Act this week, a substantial legislative proposal intended to address persistent shortcomings in online consumer protection. The initiative has been developed by Michael McGrath, the Irish commissioner responsible for justice and consumer affairs, and is widely regarded as a defining element of his mandate.

A central objective is to enhance transparency in the ticketing sector. Under the draft, platforms such as Ticketmaster would be required to disclose the number of tickets remaining and their corresponding prices. Consumers in virtual queues would consequently be informed of both the current price and the maximum price applicable. Nevertheless, the proposal is confined to disclosure obligations and does not regulate dynamic pricing comprehensively.

Comparable obligations would apply to subscription services. Providers would be obliged to notify consumers prior to the conversion of a free trial into a paid contract or prior to automatic renewal, and online cancellation procedures would need to be readily accessible.

Furthermore, the draft addresses deceptive interface design, commonly termed dark patterns, including artificial scarcity. Video game developers would be required to disclose the probability of obtaining loot box rewards, and unsubstantiated sustainability claims would be prohibited. Users would also be entitled to deactivate potentially addictive functions such as infinite scroll and autoplay.
The eventual outcome remains contingent upon negotiations with the European Parliament and the Council of the EU, which may introduce significant amendments.
sentZh: 歐盟執委會預計本週提出《數位公平法》，這是一項重大的立法提案，旨在解決網路消費者保護長期存在的不足。
這項倡議由負責司法與消費者事務的愛爾蘭籍執委麥格拉斯推動，普遍被視為其任期內的代表性工作。
核心目標之一是提升票務業的透明度。
根據草案，Ticketmaster等平台必須公開剩餘票數及相應價格。
因此，在虛擬隊伍中的消費者將得知目前價格和適用的最高價格。
不過，該提案僅限於揭露義務，並未全面規範動態定價。
類似的義務也將適用於訂閱服務。
業者必須在免費試用轉為付費合約前或自動續約前通知消費者，線上取消程序也必須便於使用。
此外，草案也處理被稱為「黑暗模式」的欺騙性介面設計，包括人為製造的稀缺感。
遊戲開發商必須公開取得戰利品箱獎勵的機率，缺乏根據的永續宣稱也將被禁止。
用戶也將有權停用無限滾動和自動播放等可能使人上癮的功能。
最終結果仍取決於與歐洲議會及歐盟理事會的協商，兩者可能做出重大修改。
